To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the PDE framework can be used to derive accelerated optimization methods for a variety of problems, that these methods can be cast into a continuum limit variational framework formulated in terms of a Bregman divergence and that this framework can be further extended to manifolds.

the PDE framework for accelerated optimization can be extended from finite dimensional manifolds to infinite dimensional manifolds and that the resulting PDEs are closely related to optimal mass transport.

(a) accelerated gradient optimization schemes for the active contour model can be formulated as a co-evolving mass transport process; (b) the resulting PDE’s can be interpreted as a continuum limit of the discrete, accelerated optimization schemes of Nesterov; and (c) the co-evolving mass models are also the continuum limits of the discrete, mass transport processes used for optimal mass transport.

accelerated optimization in the PDE framework is a new paradigm which has the potential to powerfully boost optimization performance and which is also linked to the theory of fluid dynamical optimal transport.

the proposed PDE based optimization scheme, when compared to traditional gradient-based methods, offers a significant improvement in the convergence rate, a more robust search for local minimizers, and a more natural formulation for the distributed mass case.

we show how the Bregman framework of Wibisono et al can be generalized to the infinite-dimensional setting of PDEs and that this leads to a new family of accelerated PDE-based optimization methods, which we demonstrate on a variety of examples, including the active contour case.
The main takeaway from our work is that

accelerated optimization methods may be formulated within the PDE framework and may thus be applied in a variety of contexts where traditional gradient descent fails, such as the active contour case, where the object of interest is a curve or a surface.

the variational PDE framework for accelerated optimization, while still being relatively new, already offers a rich set of mathematical tools that can be used to construct and analyze a variety of optimization schemes.

accelerated optimization methods can be cast in the PDE framework, and that the resulting continuum limit formulations are amenable to a number of extensions, including to infinite dimensional manifolds, and to a distributed mass model that co-evolves with the object of optimization.
